title: Safe-merge lifecycle: contribution gates, compatibility shims, and deprecation windows
creator: Marina Chen
description: A compact, pragmatic checklist and process for merging design system changes (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) while guaranteeing backwards compatibility, measurable telemetry, and a defined deprecation path for breaking changes.
scope: Applies to all visual tokens, primitive components (Button, Input), data components (Table, Chart), and any public exported CSS/JS helpers in the design system packages. Excludes ephemeral experimentation branches and internal utility modules not published to npm/registry.
contribution_steps: Open a lightweight RFC for any change that alters public props, token names, or default behaviours (link RFC template in links).
Run the compatibility script (scripts/compat-check) against downstream consumer snapshots and include the results in the PR description.
Create a migration snippet in the PR body demonstrating the old -> new usage for tokens and component props.
Add feature-flag guarded implementation for opt-in behaviour where feasible (env flag or package-level flag).
Add unit + visual snapshot tests and a 'compatibility test' that runs against the last 3 stable releases of the design system in CI.
Attach CI performance metrics for rendering (bundle delta, paint cost for chart redraws) if the change touches rendering code.
Obtain explicit approvals: design lead, frontend engineering reviewer, and a maintainer from the last touching area.
review_checklist: Does the change modify any exported token names, scale values, or token semantics? If yes, an RFC and migration plan is required.
Are prop names, default values, or event semantics changed? If yes, demonstrate non-breaking wrapper or provide a deprecation shim.
Have we included visual diffs (Chromatic / Percy) and confirmed no >1% visual regressions for critical pages?
Is there an automated migration codemod or example that consumers can run?
Is the change covered by unit and integration tests, and are snapshots updated intentionally?
Has the change been smoke-tested in the Canary release channel with at least two consumer apps?
Does the PR body include links to relevant design specs, figma frames, and acceptance criteria?
If the change affects accessibility, has an a11y review been completed and documented?
Is telemetry added/updated to detect adoption and regressions (events, feature flag metrics)?
Has the release note and migration guide been added to docs/ and the changelog generator?
deprecation_policy: Breaking changes are discouraged. When unavoidable, follow a staged deprecation: 1) RFC and announcement 60 days before release, 2) Deprecation shim published in the next minor release with console warnings, 3) Codemod + migration docs published concurrently, 4) 90-day adoption window where both old and new APIs are supported, 5) Final removal tagged and scheduled in release notes with a 30-day final notice. Security-critical removals may shorten windows and require security_review_required=true.
deprecation_windows: Minor token rename: announce 30 days, shim + warning in next minor, removal after 90 days
Prop behaviour change (non-security): announce 60 days, feature flagged opt-in for 1 minor release, removal after 180 days
Major API removal: announce 90 days, codemod + migration guide required, removal after 365 days
migration_examples: Token rename example: --color-primary -> --color-brand-primary. Provide alias token in vX.Y with console.warn and codemod 'npx ds-migrate tokens-rename'.
Button prop deprecate: 'size="compact"' replaced by 'compact={true}'. Provide wrapper that accepts size string and maps to compact boolean with deprecation message.
Chart API: old data prop 'series' -> new 'datasets'. Expose a datasets alias that converts series shape and emits telemetry event 'chart.datasets_migration' when used.
acceptance_criteria: RFC reviewed and merged with clear migration plan or explicit rationale for immediate removal.
PR includes compatibility test results and visual diffs attached to the PR check.
Docs updated: migration guide, changelog entry, and release notes drafted.
Telemetry events are in place to measure adoption and error rate within 72 hours of canary release.
Canary channel rollout completed with no P0 regressions reported by consumer owners.
rollout_strategy: Feature-flagged rollout in canary channel (internal apps + 2 external consumer teams).
Monitor adoption and error telemetry for 2 weeks. If error rate > 1% or visual regressions > 1% on critical pages, rollback immediately.
Progressively enable for remaining consumers by semantic version (minor -> patch) and publish migration scripts at each step.
telemetry_and_metrics: Event: ds.deprecation_warning_emitted -> counts how many consumers are seeing shim warnings.
Event: ds.migration_codmod_run -> success/failure rate for automated migrations.
Metric: visual_regression_rate (Chromatic diff percent) for critical component suites.
Metric: bundle_size_delta and render_time_ms for changed components (tracked in perf dashboard).
